view.title: Cost Optimization
view.subtitle: Track and configure the mechanisms that save you money: prompt compression and prompt caching. Auto routers live under Models + Endpoints, on the Auto-Routers tab

compression.title: Headroom prompt compression
compression.description: Headroom is a native LiteLLM guardrail that compresses your prompts before they reach the model, so you pay for fewer input tokens. The tokens it removes are priced and shown on the Usage tab as compression savings. <docs>Headroom setup docs</docs>
compression.apiBaseHint: Base URL of your Headroom compression service (LiteLLM calls its /v1/compress endpoint)
compression.apiBaseDescription: The URL where your Headroom compression service is hosted
compression.enterpriseWarning: Applying compression to all requests is available to all users. Enabling it selectively per key or team is a LiteLLM Enterprise feature. Get a trial key <pricing>here</pricing>

info.uncachedInputTokens: Input tokens you sent in this range that weren't served from or written to the cache
info.cacheHitRate: Share of your input tokens that were served from the cache
info.potentialSavings: About how much you'd save if this uncached input used prompt caching. Estimated as uncached input tokens times what your cached traffic already nets per cached token (realized cache savings, after write premiums, ÷ cache read and write tokens). Blank when caching is not currently saving anything overall.

benchmarks.title: Auto-router usage
benchmarks.adminOnly: Auto-router usage is visible to proxy admin roles only

benchmarks.breakdownUnavailable: Breakdown unavailable because some usage predates classification-cost tracking.
benchmarks.explanation: Compares your actual routed spend with the estimated cost of using only the most expensive model configured in the auto-router. It accounts for both the cache savings from staying on one model and the added cache costs from switching models. Savings are net of recorded LLM classification cost, which is included in actual spend. Classification cost per 1K turns is averaged over all auto-router turns, including those that skip classification. The range counts whole sessions that overlap it, so totals can differ slightly from the Overall tab, which buckets savings by UTC day.

shadowEval.title: Shadow eval
shadowEval.description: Blind-judge the auto-router on the real traffic of a key, team, or user (teams and users cover JWT-authenticated traffic): against the models they use today before switching, or against a fixed baseline after they have switched.

shadowEval.matchedOrBeatBaseline: Router matched or beat the baseline
shadowEval.matchedOrBeatCurrent: Router matched or beat your current model
shadowEval.costTooltip: Each arm is priced as its completion plus its own routing classifier call, measured on the same judged turns; the judge's cost is excluded from both arms
shadowEval.spendVs: {{router}} vs {{other}} on the same judged turns

results.error: Results could not be loaded. Retrying.
results.collecting: Collecting verdicts. Results appear as sampled requests are judged.
results.noVerdictsRecorded: No verdicts were recorded for this job.

direction.forward: Adoption check: key's traffic vs the router
direction.reverse: Regression check: router's picks vs a baseline

shadowEval.descriptionForward: Duplicates a sampled slice of the selected targets' traffic (keys, teams, or users) through the auto-router and has an LLM judge compare both answers blind. Each target gets its own spend budget. The router's answers are never served to users; judge calls bill to the sampled traffic's own identity.
shadowEval.descriptionReverse: Duplicates a sampled slice of the traffic the auto-router already serves against a fixed baseline model and has an LLM judge compare both answers blind. Each target gets its own spend budget. The baseline's answers are never served to users; judge calls bill to the sampled traffic's own identity.

shadowEval.reverseSingleRouter: A regression check compares one router to its baseline
shadowEval.forwardSharedRouters: Every router sees the same sampled requests, judged against the same live responses
